title: Status page config
description: What the status page checks and how it looks. See the README for every setting.

title.description: The page's heading and browser tab title, such as "Acme status".

description.description: A sentence under the heading, also used as the page's meta description.

groups.description: The order groups appear in. Groups not listed come after, in alphabetical order.

intervalMinutes.description: How often the checks run. Keep it in step with the schedule in .github/workflows/status.yml.

id.description: A short, permanent name for the target. Changing it starts its history over.

label.description: The name shown on the page. Defaults to the id.

group.description: The section the target appears in.

url.description: The address to request. It's never shown on the page, but it's in this file, so in a public repository it's public.

expectedStatus.description: The status codes that count as up. Without it, any 2xx or 3xx code does.

contains.description: Text the response has to contain to count as up. Needs the GET method.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: How long to wait before the target counts as down.

slowAfterMilliseconds.description: An answer slower than this counts as degraded.

sources.description: Status documents for the page to show instead of the built-in monitor's. Each gets a tab. To keep the monitor's too, add a source with the url "status.json".

url.description: Where to read the document. It has to allow cross-origin requests.

format.description: "firestore" reads a Firestore REST API document URL.
